minutes.headline: Select Board approved higher ambulance fees, new stop signs at two intersections, and a year-end transfer.
minutes.summary: The board heard a regional hazard mitigation plan update, then approved the fire chief's ambulance fee increase and asked for run counts in next year's budget process. It approved stop and yield signs at Main/Highland/Oak Ave and a stop sign at Flat Hill Road/Sunset Lane. It heard a long discussion of a homeowner's building permit dispute, a fiscal 2014 year-end report, and committee reports.

public_comment.topic: Supported reappointment of the dam keepers and asked the board to define the position's responsibilities, records and reporting, possibly via a task force.

Homeowner in the 78 Oak Ave permit dispute asked whether the contractor can keep pulling permits, asked for a final inspection, and urged the town to review its inspection process and consider citations.

votes.motion: Approve the ambulance fee increase effective October 1 and request run counts for prior years and 2014 in the budget process.
Approve installation of stop signs and a yield sign at Main, Highland and Oak Ave as presented.
Approve a stop sign at Flat Hill Road and Sunset Lane as presented.
Approve the transfer of $1,334 from health insurance to legal expenses.
Appoint the dam keeper, assistant dam keeper and town counsel as read by the town manager.

Local option meals tax came in well above the state's estimate.
Final transfer into legal expenses was approved by the finance committee and the board.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted, with no one opposed, to raise ambulance fees from October 1 and asked the fire chief for run counts in the next budget process.
The board approved stop signs and a yield sign at Main, Highland and Oak Ave, with no one opposed.
The board approved a stop sign at Flat Hill Road and Sunset Lane, with no one opposed.
The board approved a year-end transfer from health insurance to legal expenses, then appointed the dam keeper, assistant dam keeper and town counsel.
The board spent a long session on a homeowner's building permit dispute at 78 Oak Ave and took no vote; the building official is to bring examples of how other communities handle citations.

why_it_matters: Ambulance fees are paid by residents who use the service, and the run counts requested will show in next year's budget process how much the increase offsets the ambulance operation's loss.
The new stop and yield signs change traffic rules at two sets of intersections on Main, Highland, Oak Ave, Flat Hill Road and Sunset Lane.
Free cash, from year-end surplus, is expected to be certified and would need Town Meeting approval before it is spent, so residents may be asked to vote on it.
watch_next: The October 7th meeting, where skipped items move and a goals workshop is planned for about 6:00, town manager goals first.
The fire chief's ambulance run counts for prior years and 2014 in the next budget process.
